clue.text: Hairpiece found in London street

explanation.surface: A wig turns up somewhere in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thread of hair is a strand, and the Strand is a well-known thoroughfare in central London.

clue.text: Generate mayhem as a young person

indicators.note: mayhem is chaos, so the word is thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Adolescents notoriously cause chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen, an adolescent.

clue.text: Girl with inclination to become record producer

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A young woman with a bent for it goes into the music business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record producer' suggests the music industry; here it is someone who writes historical records.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, yearly records of events.

clue.text: Perform for free?

explanation.surface: A question about doing a gig without a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for free' suggests no payment; 'for' is a link joining two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One discharges a duty by carrying it out, and a prisoner or patient is discharged when released.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well naval rating included in plan

indicators.note: the rating's letters are put inside the word for a plan, so they are included in it

parts.note: a layout is a plan or arrangement
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual naval rating

explanation.surface: A lazy sailor gets written into somebody's scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an idle, worthless person who avoids work.

clue.text: A tailor may make money dishonestly

definitions.text: A tailor may make money dishonestly

parts.words: A tailor may make money dishonestly
parts.note: literally a tailor puts lining into the pouches of a garment; idiomatically the phrase means enriching oneself by corrupt means

explanation.surface: A dressmaker might be crooked about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to profit unfairly, as with bribes or embezzlement.

clue.text: Dissection of tiny particle, in whatever setting

indicators.note: the particle sits in the other word, placed within it
the outer word acts as a setting, like a ring around a jewel

parts.note: any means whatever, as in 'any will do'
an atom is a tiny particle of matter

explanation.surface: Cutting up a minute speck, whatever the circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy originally meant cutting up a body to study its structure.

clue.text: Rampaging lord capturing enemy is a veteran

indicators.note: one piece captures the other, holding it inside
rampaging means running wild, so the word's letters are scattered

parts.note: time is proverbially the enemy, as in 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: A rioting nobleman takes a foe prisoner, being an old soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampaging' scrambles the nobleman's title to OLDR; 'capturing' puts the enemy inside it. Time as the enemy is a stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is someone with long experience, a veteran.

clue.text: Working occasionally, with extra time, can be attractive

indicators.note: an extra letter is slipped in, added to the word for temporary work

parts.note: temping is doing temporary work now and then

explanation.surface: Part-time work with overtime can appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with extra' adds T into TEMPING, after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempting means alluring or enticing.

clue.text: Poet seen around US city decades later

indicators.note: the decades-later letters go around the city, holding it inside them

parts.note: tens are decades, groups of ten years
NY is short for New York
on, as in 'later on', means afterwards

explanation.surface: A versifier is spotted near an American city many years on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the city between the decades and 'later'; 'seen' is only a link. 'Later' gives ON as in 'later on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Haphazard part of Smollett's work

explanation.surface: A slapdash excerpt from an eighteenth-century novelist's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tobias Smollett wrote the novel Roderick Random, so the word is part of his book's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard is chance or aimless, and the surname of Smollett's hero Roderick forms half the novel's title.

clue.text: Commotion made by extremely lordly husband hugged by bear

indicators.note: the inner letters are held in the bear's arms, enclosed within its name

parts.note: Baloo is the bear in Kipling's Jungle Book

indicators.note: only the extremes of the word, its first and last letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A grand married man causes a fuss when a bear embraces him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'lordly'. The bear is Baloo from Kipling's Jungle Book, not a generic bruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss or hype, a synonym for a big commotion.

clue.text: In danger of punishment, pinching new European money

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: someone 'for it' is about to be punished

explanation.surface: A thief in line for a penalty after stealing fresh foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR IT is British slang for being in trouble; N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is Hungary's currency unit.

clue.text: No hooter is so harsh and high-pitched

definitions.text: No hooter is so harsh and high-pitched

parts.words: No hooter is so harsh and high-pitched
parts.note: the barn owl is called the screech owl because it shrieks rather than hoots, so no hooting owl sounds that shrill

explanation.surface: No owl's call is as grating and shrill as this one.
explanation.definitionFit: A screechy voice is harsh and shrill, like the cry of the screech owl.

clue.text: Judge hirsute growth to be source of anguish

parts.note: a judge hears a case, so to hear is to judge
tache is short for moustache

explanation.surface: Judge a man's moustache and cause him distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is grief or emotional pain, a cause of sorrow.

clue.text: Make cross as heraldic device

explanation.surface: Annoy someone, as a coat of arms might.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to vex or irritate, and in heraldry a fret is a charge of interlaced bands.

clue.text: Struggle to get fish

explanation.surface: Fight hard to land a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to stumble or struggle helplessly, and the flounder is a flatfish.

clue.text: Industrial waste loaded after change of leader

indicators.note: the word's leading letter, its first, is swapped for another

parts.note: loaded is slang for rich, affluent

explanation.surface: Factory pollution piles up after a new boss arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of AFFLUENT changes from A to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluent is liquid waste discharged from factories or sewage works.

clue.text: What a bore for the hunt!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of tedium from someone off to ride with hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A drag hunt follows an artificial scent trail laid by dragging a lure, rather than a live fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is a drag, and a drag is also the scent trail or the hunt that follows it.

clue.text: Exhaustive legal document about limitation of ownership

indicators.note: the document goes about the other piece, surrounding it

parts.note: a deed is a legal document conveying property
a tail, or fee tail, limits who may inherit an estate

explanation.surface: A thorough contract covers restricted property rights.
explanation.walkthrough: In property law a tail (entail) restricts inheritance to particular heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Detailed means thorough, covering every point.

clue.text: Forbear to be found high up a tree

definitions.text: Forbear to be found high up a tree

parts.words: Forbear to be found high up a tree
parts.note: a forebear appears in the upper branches of a family tree, not a leafy one; 'Forbear' looks like a verb meaning refrain

explanation.surface: Refrain from being discovered in the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is a forefather, someone from whom you descend.

clue.text: Habitually stock Japanese drink as a souvenir

parts.note: a shop that keeps an item stocks it regularly
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A shop always carries rice wine to sell as a memento.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is something kept to remind you of a person or place, like a souvenir.

clue.text: Flier making way over river in boat

indicators.note: the way and river letters sit in the boat, inside its letters

parts.note: keel is an old word for a flat-bottomed boat

indicators.note: in a down clue the way goes over, so above, the river

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A bird crosses a river by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keel' as a boat is an old word for a flat-bottomed barge, chiefly northern English; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Loose hair over eye singular girl cut first

indicators.note: the shortened name is to come first in the answer, before the hair
the girl's name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Una is a girl's name, and 'una' means one, hence singular
a lash is a hair growing on the eyelid

explanation.surface: Stray hair falls over a girl's eye after a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the girl's name of its last letter, and 'first' sends what is left ahead of the hair. Una is Latin and Spanish for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlash is to untie, setting something loose.

clue.text: Country dweller disposed to get car

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone in the countryside is inclined to buy a motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager is someone who lives in a rural cottage.

clue.text: Colourless and boring, though holding attention

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it, so these letters wrap around the second

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A dull speaker still somehow commands an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and drab, lacking colour or interest.

clue.text: Wrongly let a case develop by stages

indicators.note: wrongly signals these letters are set out incorrectly and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A lawsuit allowed to proceed in error grows step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to increase or intensify in steps.

clue.text: Hard-hearted book? Not so

parts.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Is a book cruel? Apparently not that much.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means showing no pity, merciless.

clue.text: Go through ruin by river

parts.note: end, as in 'be the end of', means ruin or destruction
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Suffer devastation beside a watercourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to undergo or suffer something, to go through it.
